source: ‘Documentation for the D&BP Act — An Architectural Design Practitioner’s Perspective’, presentation to the NSW Building Commission (GWH). Benchmarked against the Class 2 Macquarie Tower and Class 3 Hudson Ave document sets, which the Commission holds up as examples of good-quality documentation.
purpose: The drawing series a complete, declarable Class 2/3/9c set is expected to contain, grouped by DBP regulated building element. A missing series is itself a defect: the Building Practitioner cannot build a regime that was never documented, and the design cannot be 'in a form suitable for construction'.

regimes.label: General / Architectural
plans: Coversheet (drawing register for the set + site and building details)
Site Plan (building in the context of the site, boundaries, fire source features, reduced levels)
Grid Setout Plan (dimensioned, with grids and survey points)
General Arrangement Plans (each level, including roof and basements)
General Sections (at least two intersecting sections)
Sections through driveway, other ramps and egress

regimes.label: Fire Safety Systems
plans: Wall Setout Plans / Party Wall Setout Plans

regimes.label: Waterproofing
plans: Waterproofing Floor Gradient / Floor Waste Plans

regimes.label: Building Enclosure
plans: Waterproofing Floor Gradient / Floor Waste Plans — Roof
External Waterproofing Detail Call Out Plans — Roof
Basement Wall Construction Plans (waterstops to basement walls/piling, tanking/waterproofing to basement walls)
Schedule Call Out Plans — Ground Floor Facade Brick Coursing
details: Weatherproofing of external walls for all facade types
External flashing details (called out from the general set)
External wall and floor/balcony interface details (called out from the general set)
Interface between different external wall building materials

regimes.label: Building Services
plans: Reflected Ceiling Plans (coordinated with fire, mechanical, electrical and hydraulic)

expectations: A named coordination leader — architect, consultant or external design manager — who sets timelines, goals and accountability.
Coordination carried out in 3D so vertical and horizontal clashes and service routes are resolved before construction.
A maintained design coordination register so items are demonstrably closed out.
Modelling expectations set per discipline via an LOD requirement or BIM Management Plan.

lod.LOD 100: Symbol or generic representation; information may be derived from other elements.
lod.LOD 200: Conceptual/schematic — generic system, object or assembly with approximate quantity, size, shape, location, orientation.
lod.LOD 300: Detailed design — specific system, object or assembly with quantity, size, shape, location and orientation.
lod.LOD 350: As LOD 300 plus interfaces with other building systems. This is the practical floor for construction documentation.
lod.LOD 400: Fabrication and assembly — includes detailing, fabrication, assembly and installation information.

knownGaps: There is little published material showing what good-quality documentation actually looks like, so sets are usually corrected only by being told what is wrong.
2D documentation frequently fails to make complicated junctions legible; 3D models / digital twins resolve what plans and sections cannot.
‘Suitable for construction’ has no widely understood quantifiable benchmark — which is why detail scale, callouts and integration must be checked explicitly rather than assumed.
